BURSEVI:v10p318/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p318/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p318/r6.claim: The earlier scrolls include those of Abraham and Moses; sahifa means a sheet or written page, while mushaf is a collection of written sheets.
BURSEVI:v10p318/r6.anchor: {صحف} جدك {إبراهيم} الخليل عليه السلام صحف أخيك {موسى} الكليم عليه السلام بدل من الصحف الأولى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says this sura was copied from the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : ان هذا لفي الصحف الاولى قال : نسخت هذه السورة من صحف إبراهيم وموسى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says this sura appears in Abraham's and Moses' scriptures just as it was revealed to Muhammad.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r2.anchor: عن السدى ان هذه السورة في صحف إبراهيم وموسى مثل ما نزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the story of this sura is found in the earlier scriptures.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه ان هذا لفي الصحف الاولى يقول : قصة هذه السورة في الصحف الاولى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r4.claim: Qatada says God's books came successively with the message that the Hereafter is better and more enduring.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه ان هذا لفي الصحف الاولى قال : تتابعت كتب الله كما تسمعون ان الاخرة خير وابقى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r5.claim: Qatada also says the earlier scriptures taught that the Hereafter is better than the world.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه ان هذا لفي الصحف الاولى الاية قال : في الصحف الاولى ان الاخرة خير من الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says this teaching is in all God's books.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3419#2/r6.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه ان هذا لفي الصحف الاولى قال : في كتب الله كلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r3.claim: The closing statement dignifies this beneficial, enduring teaching as also found in Abraham's and Moses' scriptures, emphasized for deniers familiar with those messengers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r3.anchor: تذييل للكلام وتنويه به بأنه من الكلام النافع الثابت في كتب إبراهيم وموسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r4.claim: “This” refers to the teaching from success through the afterlife's superiority; the earlier opening verses are not what the old scriptures confirm here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r4.anchor: والإشارة بكلمة { هذا } إلى مجموع قوله { قد أفلح من تزكى إلى قوله وأبقى } ( الأعلى : 14 17 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r5.claim: Ibn Mardawayh and al-Ajurri report Abu Dharr asking the Prophet about revelation from Abraham's and Moses' scrolls; the Prophet recited 87:14–17, and Ibn Ashur could not establish the report's grade.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r5.anchor: روى ابن مردويه والآجري عن أبي ذر قال : ( قلت يا رسول الله هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ؟

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r7.claim: Ṣuḥuf is an irregular plural of ṣaḥīfa but the more eloquent form; Abraham had scrolls, while Moses had many, comprising the Torah's books.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r7.anchor: و { الصحف } : جمع صحيفة على غير قياس لأن قياس جمعه صحائف ، ولكنه مع كونه غير مقيس هو الأفصح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r8.claim: The wording moves from a general mention to specification: “the scrolls of Abraham and Moses” apposes “the earlier scrolls.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p290/r8.anchor: وجاء نظم الكلام على أسلوب الإجمال والتفصيل ليكون لهذا الخبر مزيد تقرير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r20.speaker: أبو رجاء، ابن الزبير، أبو موسى الأشعري، عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r20.claim: The source records variant pronunciations of Ibrahim: Abu Raja drops yā and alif; Ibn Zubayr and Abu Musa use Ibraham; Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra has kasra on hāʾ and omits yā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r20.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء: إبراهيم بغير الياء ولا ألف، وقرأ ابن الزبير «ابراهام» في كل القرآن،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r21.claim: A report dates the revealed scriptures to Ramadan: Abraham's on night one, Torah on night six, Psalms on night twelve, Gospel on night eighteen, and Quran on night fourteen.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p470#2/r21.anchor: وروي أن صحف إبراهيم نزلت في أول ليلة من رمضان، والتوراة في السادسة من رمضان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p93/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p93/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p93/r1.claim: The earlier scriptures are identified as the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; they were also discussed at 53:36.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p93/r1.anchor: ثم بين الصحف الأولى ما هي فقال

JISHUMI:v10p7380/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r9.claim: The earlier scriptures are the books of Abraham and Moses.
JISHUMI:v10p7380/r9.anchor: الصحف الأولى أي: كتب الأولين صحف إبراهيم وموسى كتابهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r1.claim: This may refer to the teaching from success through the better, lasting Hereafter, or to the entire surah; its meaning is found in earlier scriptures.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى قوله : { قد أفلح } إلى { أبقى }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r2.speaker: أبو ذر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r2.claim: Abu Dharr reports asking the Prophet about scriptures; the reply counts 104, apportioned among Adam, Seth, Enoch, Abraham, and the four later named books.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه ( أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says Abraham's scroll teaches a prudent person to guard his tongue, know his time, and attend to his affairs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r3.anchor: في صحف إبراهيم ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه مقبلا على شأنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r4.claim: A prophetic report promises ten rewards for each letter God revealed to Abraham, Moses, and Muhammad to whoever recites al-A'la.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة الأعلى أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد كل حرف أنزله الله على إبراهيم وموسى ومحمد

MUQATIL:87:14-19/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:87:14-19/r4.claim: The teaching is found in the earlier scriptures: Ibrahim's scrolls and the books of Moses, meaning the Torah; Ibrahim's scrolls have since been taken away.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#8/r1.claim: “The earlier scriptures” is specified by apposition as the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#8/r2.claim: An aphorism attributed to Abraham's scriptures says a wise person should guard his tongue, know his time, and attend to his own affairs.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p333#8/r2.anchor: وفى الأثر وفى صحف إبراهيم ينبغى للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه

QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r6.claim: The scrolls are revelations sent to Abraham and Moses; the claim is that their meaning occurs there, not that these exact words do.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:18-19/r6.anchor: يعني الكتب المنزلة عليهما. ولم يرد أن هذه الألفاظ بعينها في تلك الصحف

NAHHAS:v5p207/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p207/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p207/r18.claim: Ṣuḥuf is an appositional substitute, and ṣaḥīfa means a book.

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r1.claim: The surah's foundational creed is ancient, rooted in the first scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r1.anchor: هذا الذي ورد في هذه السورة وهو يتضمن أصول العقيدة الكبرى

QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r2.claim: Truth and creed are one because their source and the will behind sending messengers are one; details vary with changing needs and eras but return to the same root.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:18/r2.anchor: إنه حق واحد ، يرجع إلى أصل واحد

QUTB-ZILAL:87:19/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:19/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:19/r1.claim: The core truths of this surah were present in Abraham's and Moses' scriptures; the creed's shared source is the Lord who creates, perfects, apportions, and guides.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:19/r1.anchor: إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى

RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r1.claim: The words identify which earlier scriptures are meant by the preceding phrase.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنه بيان لقوله : { فى الصحف الاولى }

RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r2.claim: Alternatively, the teaching appears in the scriptures of all prophets; a report from Abu Dharr lists 104 revealed books, including the ten given to Abraham.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r2.anchor: روي عن أبي ذر أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كم أنزل الله من كتاب ؟

RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r3.claim: A saying attributed to Abraham’s scrolls advises the wise to guard the tongue, know the age, and attend to one’s own affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v31p135#4/r3.anchor: في صحف إبراهيم : ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه مقبلا على شأنه

SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r1.claim: The common reading of Ibrāhīm has alif after rāʾ and yāʾ after hāʾ; Abū Rajāʾ omits both, with either fatḥa or kasra on hāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r1.anchor: قرأ العامة بألف بعد الراء وياء بعد الهاء، وأبو رجاء بحذفهما

SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r2.speaker: أبو موسى وابن الزبير
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r2.claim: Abū Mūsā and Ibn al-Zubayr read the name with two alifs throughout the Qur'an.
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r2.anchor: وأبو موسى وابن الزبير بألفين وكذا في كل القرآن

SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r3.speaker: مالك ابن دينار
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r3.claim: Mālik b. Dīnār reads only the alif after rāʾ and opens hāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r3.anchor: ومالك ابن دينار بألف بعد الراء فقط، والهاء مفتوحة

SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكر
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r4.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Bakr omits the alif and reads hāʾ with kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r4.anchor: وعبد الرحمن بن أبي بكر " وإبراهيم " بحذف الألف وكسر الهاء

SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r5.speaker: ابن خالويه
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r5.claim: Ibn Khālawayh also records Ibrāham, with an alif and ḍamma on hāʾ; the author says the name's forms were fully discussed in al-Baqara.
SAMIN-DURR:87:19/r5.anchor: وقال ابن خالويه: " وقد جاء " إبراهم " يعني بألف وضم الهاء.

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r1.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r1.claim: The reference to old scriptures may concern the subjects discussed in verses 14–17.
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r1.anchor: This refers to either the subjects mentioned in vv. 14–17

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that it refers to the whole of this surah.

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r3.speaker: Āl
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r3.claim: Another interpretation applies the reference to the entire Quran, as verse 26:196 does.
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r3.anchor: or the entire Quran, as in 26:196

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r4.claim: Although Judaism and Christianity do not assign Abraham a revealed book, the Quran and hadith imply that he had a scripture.
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r4.anchor: Although Judaism and Christianity do not ascribe a revealed book to Abraham, that Abraham had a particular scripture is implied in both the Quran and the Ḥadīth

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r5.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r5.claim: A report attributes to the Prophet a total of 104 revealed books: 50 to Seth, 30 to Idrīs, 10 to Abraham, 10 to Moses before the Torah, plus Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Quran.
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r5.anchor: When the Prophet was asked how many revealed books there were, he responded

STUDYQURAN:87:18/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r6.speaker: Shiite sources
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r6.claim: Shiite sources give a slightly different narration, and some say Abraham received 20 scrolls.
STUDYQURAN:87:18/r6.anchor: This tradition has a slightly different narration in Shiite sources

TAB:87:19/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:87:19/r1.claim: ʿIkrima takes this to refer to the verses in Sūrat al-Aʿlā.
TAB:87:19/r1.anchor: عن عكرِمة إنّ هَذَا لفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى صُحُفِ إبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى يقول :  الاَيات التي في سبح اسم ربك الأعلى .

TAB:87:19/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB:87:19/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the story of the whole sūrah was already in the earlier scriptures.
TAB:87:19/r2.anchor: عن أبي العالية إن هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى صُحُفِ إبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى قال :  قصة هذه السورة لفي الصحف الأولى .

TAB:87:19/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:19/r3.claim: Qatāda interprets the reference as what God related in this sūrah being present in the earlier pages.
TAB:87:19/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ،   في قوله :  إنّ هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى قال :  إن هذا الذي قصّ الله في هذه السورة

TAB:87:19/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:19/r4.claim: Qatāda also says God's books agree that the afterlife is better and more enduring.
TAB:87:19/r4.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  إنّ هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى قال :  تتابعت كتب الله كما تسمعون

TAB:87:19/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:87:19/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the pages given to Abraham and Moses taught that the afterlife is better than the first life.
TAB:87:19/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  إنّ هَذَا لَفِي الصّحُفِ الأُولى صُحُفِ إبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى قال :  في الصحف

TAB:87:19/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r6.speaker: author
TAB:87:19/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the demonstrative covers the nearby verses about purification, prayer, preferring this life, and the better, lasting afterlife, since this is the nearest referent; ṣuḥuf means the books of Abraham and Moses.
TAB:87:19/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب ،   قول من قال :  إن قوله :  قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكى وَذَكَرَ اسمَ رَبّهِ فَصَلّى

TAB:87:19/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r7.speaker: author
TAB:87:19/r7.claim: Ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfa, and here means the books of Abraham and Moses.
TAB:87:19/r7.anchor: وأما الصحف :  فإنها جمع صحيفة ،   وإنما عُنِي بها :  كتب إبراهيم وموسى .

TAB:87:19/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:19/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:19/r8.claim: Qatāda reports a chronology in which Abraham's pages came on Ramadan's first night, the Torah on the sixth, Psalms on the twelfth, Gospel on the eighteenth, and Qur'an on the twenty-fourth.
TAB:87:19/r8.anchor: عن أبي الخلد ،   قال :  نزلت صحف إبراهيم في أوّل ليلة من رمضان ،   وأنزلت التوراة لستّ ليال

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r4.claim: Calling the scriptures ancient before naming Abraham and Moses is said to magnify their status.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r4.anchor: وفي إبهام الصحف ووصفها بالتقدم أولا ثم بيانها وتفسيرها بصحف إبراهيم وموسى

TABATABAI:87:19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:19/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:87:19/r1.claim: In a report from Abū Dharr, the Prophet answers whether revelation contains anything from Abraham’s and Moses’ scrolls by reciting 87:14–19, supporting the author’s broader referent for “this.”
TABATABAI:87:19/r1.anchor: عن أبي ذر في حديث قلت يا رسول الله فما في الدنيا مما أنزل الله عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى؟ قال يا أبا ذر اقرأ

TABATABAI:87:19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:19/r2.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:87:19/r2.claim: Al-Ṣādiq tells Abū Baṣīr that the community possesses the scrolls named as Abraham’s and Moses’ scriptures, and confirms that these are the tablets.
TABATABAI:87:19/r2.anchor: وفي البصائر بإسناده عن أبي بصير قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام عندنا الصحف التي قال الله { صحف إبراهيم وموسى }

TABATABAI:87:19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:19/r3.claim: He understands the tablets as the Torah, which the Qurʾān also calls tablets in its accounts of Moses.
TABATABAI:87:19/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بكون الصحف هي الألواح كونها هي التوراة المعبر عنها في مواضع من القرآن بالألواح

TABATABAI:87:19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:19/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:87:19/r4.claim: Abū Dharr reports the Prophet’s account of 124,000 prophets, 313 messengers, four Arab prophets, and 104 revealed books, including ten sheets to Abraham; another transmission omits Adam’s sheets and adds ten sheets for Moses.

TABRISI:87:18-19/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:18-19/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:18-19/r3.claim: The first scrolls are the scriptures of Abraham and Moses; this supports the view that Abraham received a revealed book.
TABRISI:87:18-19/r3.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أن إبراهيم كان قد أنزل عليه الكتاب خلافا لمن يزعم أنه لم ينزل عليه كتاب

TABRISI:87:18-19/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:18-19/r4.speaker: أبو ذر، النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:87:18-19/r4.claim: In a report from Abū Dharr, the Prophet counts 124,000 prophets, 313 messengers, and 104 revealed books distributed among Adam, Seth, Enoch, Abraham, and the four named scriptures.
TABRISI:87:18-19/r4.anchor: وروي عن أبي ذر أنه قال قلت يا رسول الله كم الأنبياء فقال

TABRISI:87:18-19/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:18-19/r5.speaker: إبراهيم
TABRISI:87:18-19/r5.claim: A saying in Abraham's scrolls urges a wise person to guard the tongue, know the age, and attend to personal affairs.
TABRISI:87:18-19/r5.anchor: ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه مقبلا على شأنه

TABRISI:87:18-19/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:18-19/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:18-19/r6.claim: Another report says all of God's scriptures were sent down during Ramadan.
TABRISI:87:18-19/r6.anchor: إن كتب الله كلها أنزلت في شهر رمضان

THALABI:v10p185/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r8.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v10p185/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the referent is the Qurʾān, which is in the earlier books, namely the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
THALABI:v10p185/r8.anchor: الضحاك: إن هذا القرآن، لفي الصحف الكتب الأولى

THALABI:v10p185/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p185/r11.speaker: أبو ذر
THALABI:v10p185/r11.claim: Abū Dharr's report begins with the Prophet saying there were 124,000 prophets and 313 messengers, including four Arab prophets: Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Shuʿayb, and Muḥammad.
THALABI:v10p185/r11.anchor: قلت: يا رسول الله كم الأنبياء؟ قال: «مائة ألف وأربعة وعشرون ألفا

THALABI:v10p186/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p186/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
THALABI:v10p186/r1.claim: The Prophet's report to Abū Dharr says 104 books were revealed: ten sheets to Adam, fifty to Seth, thirty to Enoch/Idrīs, ten to Abraham, plus Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and the Furqān; Idrīs was first to write with a pen.
THALABI:v10p186/r1.anchor: مائة وأربع كتب، منها على آدم عشر صحف، وعلى شيث خمسين صحيفة، وعلى أخنوخ، وهو إدريس

ASAD-NOTES:87:18#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:18#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:87:18#n9/r1.claim: Abraham and Moses exemplify earlier revelations, underscoring continuity in religious experience and the shared basic truths of all prophets.
ASAD-NOTES:87:18#n9/r1.anchor: These two names are given here only as examples of earlier prophetic revelations

ASAD-NOTES:87:18#n9/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:18#n9/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:87:18#n9/r2.claim: Suhuf literally means leaves or scrolls and is synonymous with kitab, so Asad renders it as revelations.
ASAD-NOTES:87:18#n9/r2.anchor: The noun suhuf (sing. sahifah), which literally denotes "leaves [of a book]" or "scrolls"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p450/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p450/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p450/r5.claim: The scrolls are books revealed to Abraham; Moses also received scrolls before the Torah, though “Moses’ scrolls” may mean the Torah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p450/r5.anchor: يريد كتبا أنزلت على إبراهيم، وكان نزل على موسى صحف

WAHIDI-QT:87:19/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:19/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:19/r1.claim: The scrolls of Abraham and Moses are the books God revealed to them.
WAHIDI-QT:87:19/r1.anchor: يعني ما أنزل الله عليهما من الكتب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:17-19/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:17-19/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:17-19/r3.claim: The earlier scriptures meant here are the books revealed to Abraham and Moses.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:17-19/r3.anchor: يعني: ما أنزل الله عليهما من الكتب.

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r1.claim: The formula about Abraham’s and Moses’ scrolls parallels Q 53:36–37; the note also points to the general discussion of Moses in the early Meccan Quran.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r1.anchor: zu der Wendung ṣuḥuf ʾibrāhīm wa-mūsā vgl. 53:36.37

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r2.claim: Though readings closer to biblical forms exist, Horovitz’s reasoning supports Ibrāhīm as correct: it parallels Ismāʿīl and is used by Umayya b. Abī ṣ-Ṣalt.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Mit Horovitz 1925, 16, ist jedoch davon auszugehen, dass die in Analogie zu Ismāʿīl gebildete Form Ibrāhīm korrekt ist

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Ahrens
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r3.claim: Ahrens interprets the scrolls as a rough designation for the Old Testament or the whole Bible because Q 53:36 onward paraphrases biblical material.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Ahrens will die „Schriften Abrahams und Moses“ als „eine ungefähre Bezeichnung des Alten Testaments oder vielmehr der ganzen Bibel“ verstehen

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r4.claim: Despite Abraham not receiving a revealed book in the Old Testament, the pair may summarize biblical scripture through the figures’ prominence; specific apocryphal Abrahamic books are unlikely.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Wie in Q 53 ist vermutlich weniger eine Evokation bestimmter biblischer Einzelschriften intendiert

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r5.speaker: Heck
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r5.claim: Heck likewise reads the genitive objectively, as revealed writings about Moses and Abraham; the author instead sees a broad evocation of biblical tradition rather than specific books.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r5.anchor: Heck, „Scrolls“, EQ, der den Genitiv ebenfalls im Sinne eines Genitivus objectivus als über Mose und Abraham berichtende Offenbarungsschriften deutet

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r6.claim: Ṣuḥuf means documents or written sheets, likely borrowed from Old South Arabian; in early Quranic usage its plural names revelation texts or a heavenly archetype, unlike profane pre-Islamic poetry.

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r7.claim: Later occurrences at Q 20:133 and 98:2 appear to quote early passages; from Mecca II kitāb replaces ṣuḥuf as the usual term for revelation scripture, alongside zubur.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r7.anchor: Ab Mekka II wird der Ausdruck ṣuḥuf durch das arabische Wort kitāb verdrängt

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r9.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r9.claim: The repeated scroll term links verses 18–19 by concatenation, a device also found in early Quranic passages and pre-Islamic poetry that stretches syntax across short verses.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:18-19:anmerkung/r9.anchor: Zu der V. 18.19 verbindenden Konkatenation, bei der das Schlusswort eines Verses zu Beginn des folgenden Verses wieder aufgenommen wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r3.claim: The ending authorizes the rebuke by affirming that Quranic proclamation agrees with ancient revealed scriptures associated with Abraham and Moses; the psalm-like opening hymn supports this claim.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:16-19:kommentar/r3.anchor: Das Scheltwort in V. 16.17 erfährt eine nachträgliche Autorisierung durch das abschließende Verspaar V. 18.19

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r1.claim: Suhuf is the plural of sahifa, then used synonymously with book, meaning revelation given to prophets; here it refers to books given to Abraham and Moses, examples rather than the limits of revelation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r1.anchor: her iki âyette yer alan suhuftan maksat, “Hz. İbrâhim ve Hz. Mûsâ’ya verilen kitaplardır. Bu iki peygambere nisbet edilen sahîfeler, geçmiş vahiylerin sadece birer örneğini teşkil eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r2.claim: The principal named scriptures are the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Qur’an; reports assign ten sheets to Adam, fifty to Seth, thirty to Idris, and ten to Abraham.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r2.anchor: Sahîfelerden 10’unun Hz. Âdem’e, 50’sinin Şît’e, 30’unun İdrîs’e, 10’unun da İbrâhim’e verildiği rivayet edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r3.claim: As in 26:196, these verses affirm that revelation to all prophets comes from one divine source and that revealed religions share universal principles of faith, worship, and morality.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:18/r3.anchor: bütün peygamberlere vahyin tek kaynaktan, Allah’tan geldiğini ve ilâhî dinlerin iman, ibadet ve ahlâk konularında aynı prensipleri

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r1.claim: “The scrolls of Abraham and Moses” apposes the earlier scrolls; first leaving them vague and ancient, then identifying them magnifies their standing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r1.anchor: صحف إبراهيم وموسى بدل من الصحف الأولى وفي إبهامها ووصفها بالقدم ثم بيانها وتفسيرها من تفخيم شأنها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r2.claim: Abraham had ten scrolls, and Moses had ten before the Torah; these scrolls mean the latter set, excluding the Torah.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r2.anchor: وكانت صحف إبراهيم عشرة وكذا موسى صحف عليه السلام والمراد بها ما عدا التوراة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r3.claim: A report from Abū Dharr says God sent 104 books: fifty to Seth, thirty to Idrīs, ten to Abraham, ten to Moses before the Torah, then the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Furqān; al-Ālūsī leaves its authenticity to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r3.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد وابن مردويه وابن عساكر عن أبي ذر قال قلت يا رسول الله كم أنزل الله تعالى من كتاب قال مائة كتاب وأربعة كتب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r4.speaker: أبو ذر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r4.claim: The report says Abraham's scrolls were entirely parables, including God's warning to a deceived ruler that he was commissioned to answer the oppressed person's plea, even from a disbeliever.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r4.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله فما كانت صحف إبراهيم قال أمثال كلها أيها الملك المتسلط على المبتلي المغرور لم أبعثك لتجمع الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r5.speaker: أبو ذر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r5.claim: Abraham's scrolls counsel the wise to reserve time for communion with God, self-accounting and reflection, and lawful personal needs, which refreshes the other hours and heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r5.anchor: وعلى العاقل ما لم يكن مغلوبا على عقله أن يكون له ثلاث ساعات ساعة يناجي فيها ربه وساعة يحاسب فيها نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r6.speaker: أبو ذر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r6.claim: They also advise being alert to one's age, attending to one's affairs, and guarding the tongue because speech counts as deeds, so little should be said except what matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r6.anchor: وعلى العاقل أن يكون بصيرا بزمانه مقبلا على شأنه حافظا للسانه فإن من حسب كلامه من عمله أقل الكلام إلا فيما يعنيه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r7.speaker: أبو ذر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r7.claim: The same report says a wise person seeks three things: provision for livelihood, provision for the afterlife, and permissible enjoyment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r7.anchor: وعلى العاقل أن يكون طالبا لثلاث مرمة لمعاش أو تزود لمعاد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r8.speaker: أبو ذر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r8.claim: Moses's scrolls were admonitions: the certain of death yet joyful, Hell yet laughing, the world's changes yet content with it, decree yet angry, and reckoning yet inactive are all astonishing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r8.anchor: قال كانت عبرا كلها عجبت لمن أيقن بالموت ثم يفرح ولمن أيقن بالنار ثم يضحك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r9.speaker: أبو ذر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r9.claim: When asked whether any of those teachings had been revealed to him, the Prophet answered yes and recited 87:14–17.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r9.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى قال يا أبا ذر نعم قد أفلح من تزكى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r10.speaker: أبو رجاء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r10.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads Ibrāhīm with alif and yāʾ omitted and an open hāʾ; Masūra and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Bakra have other hāʾ-vowel variants.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء إبرهم بحذف الألف والياء وبالهاء مفتوحة ومسورة وعبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة بكسرها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r11.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري وابن الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r11.claim: Abū Mūsā and Ibn al-Zubayr read the name Ibrāhām throughout the Qur'an.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو موسى الأشعري وابن الزبير إبراهام بالغين في كل القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r12.speaker: مالك بن دينار
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r12.claim: Mālik b. Dīnār reads Ibrāhim with an alif and open hāʾ but no yāʾ; Ibn Khālawayh also records a form with no alif or yāʾ and a damma on hāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r12.anchor: وقرأ مالك بن دينار إبراهم بألف وفتح الهاء وبغير ياء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r13.speaker: ابن خالويه
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r13.claim: Ibn Khālawayh records the form Ibruhum with hāʾ damma and neither alif nor yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r13.anchor: وجاء كما قال ابن خالويه إبرهم بضم الهاء بلا ألف ولا ياء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r14.claim: These variants reflect Arab adaptation of foreign names; the sounder view is that Abraham is foreign. Al-Kirmānī instead derives it from Arabic barhama, intense looking.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r14.anchor: وهذا من تصرفات العرب في الأسماء الأعجمية فإن إبراهيم على الصحيح منها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r15.speaker: الكرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r15.claim: Al-Kirmānī's Wonders claims Ibrāhīm is Arabic, derived from barhama, meaning intense looking.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r15.anchor: وحكى الكرماني في عجائبه أنه اسم عربي مشتق من البرهمة وهي شدة النظر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r16.claim: Moses's lineage has already been given in the commentary.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#3/r16.anchor: ونسبه قد تقدم وكذا نسب موسى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#4/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Ghāshiya is Meccan by consensus and has 26 verses by consensus; the Prophet recited it on Friday with another sūrah, according to reports from al-Nuʿmān b. Bashīr.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p111#4/r1.anchor: مكية بلا خلاف وعدة آياتها ست وعشرون كذلك وكان صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كما أخرج مسلم داود والنسائي وابن ماجه عن النعمان بن بشير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r1.claim: ‘This’ refers to the preceding four verses: the earlier scriptures taught that the purified and praying prosper, people favor worldly life, and the afterlife is better and more lasting.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r1.anchor: ما ذكر من قوله: "قد أفلح من تزكى"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r2.claim: Ikrima and al-Suddi say this entire surah is found in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r2.anchor: قال عكرمة والسدي: هذه السورة في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r3.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet recited al-Aʿla and al-Kafirun in the two rakʿas before witr, then al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and al-Nas in witr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p403#2/r3.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:19/r1.claim: The reference to Abraham's and Moses' scriptures is an appositional explanation of the earlier scriptures.

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:19/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:19/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:19/r2.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for every letter God revealed to Abraham, Moses, and Muhammad to whoever recites this sura.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:19/r2.anchor: من قرأ سورة الأعلى أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد كل حرف أنزله الله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r1.claim: This refers to the great admonition of glorification, purification, remembrance, prayer, and turning from the world toward the afterlife; it gathers all good and belongs to every revealed law, so its aim cannot be abrogated.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r1.anchor: أي الوعظ العظيم بالتسبيح الذي ذكر في هذه السور وما تأثر عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r2.claim: The Quran preserves unsurpassed eloquence, genres of poetry, legal limits, and unseen knowledge, surpassing poets and soothsayers and showing Muhammad follows earlier messengers.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r2.anchor: فإن القرآن جمع المديح الفائق والنسيب الرقيق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r3.claim: Abraham's scrolls come first because they are closer to admonition, as the report of Abu Dharr indicates; Moses' book comes last because it chiefly contains laws and fewer admonitions.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r3.anchor: قدمه لأن صحفه أقرب إلى الوعظ كما نطق به حديث أبي ذر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r4.claim: The order also follows the prophets' historical existence and precedence in merit; Moses' scrolls contain severe warnings and the glad tidings of Muhammad.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r4.anchor: ذكر النبيين عليهما الصلاة والسلام على الأصل في ترتيب الوجود والأفضلية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.claim: Ending with purification returns to the beginning's glorification and soul-cleansing; God does not leave creation without guidance or create them purposelessly.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.anchor: وكان في إتيانه والتذكير به إعلام بأن الله تعالى لم يهمل الخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p404/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404/r1.claim: The sura explains the end of Sabbih by affirming the afterlife, beginning with the Overwhelming Event, describing the fates of the pious and wicked, and demonstrating God's power over it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404/r1.anchor: من تنزيه الله سبحانه وتعالى عن العبث بإثبات الدار الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#s088/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#s088/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#s088/r1.claim: The sura explains the end of Sabbih by affirming the afterlife, beginning with the Overwhelming Event, describing the fates of the pious and wicked, and demonstrating God's power over it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p404#s088/r1.anchor: من تنزيه الله سبحانه وتعالى عن العبث بإثبات الدار الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when the verses were revealed, the Prophet said the whole message was in Abraham’s and Moses’s scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r4.anchor: قال: لما نزلت {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى} قال: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: هي كلها في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this sūra is in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; one version includes the end of sūra 53 as well.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} قال: نسخت هذه السورة من صحف إبراهيم وموسى

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says this sūra was present in Abraham’s and Moses’s scrolls as it was revealed to the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r6.anchor: عن السدي أن هذه السورة في صحف إبراهيم وموسى مثل ما نزلت على النبي

DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the story of this sūra appears in the earlier scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v8p487#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} يقول: قصة هذه السورة في الصحف الأولى

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the message is found in all of God’s books.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r1.anchor: {إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى} قال: في كتب الله كلها

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r2.claim: In Abū Dharr’s report, the Prophet counts 104 revealed books: fifty to Seth, thirty to Idrīs, ten to Abraham, ten to Moses before the Torah, then the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Qurʾān.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r2.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه قال: قلت يا رسول الله كم أنزل الله من كتاب قال مائة كتاب وأربعة كتب

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r3.claim: The Prophet describes Abraham’s scrolls as collections of maxims: a ruler must answer the oppressed, and a rational person divides time among worship, self-accounting, and lawful needs.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r3.anchor: فما كانت صحف إبراهيم قال: أمثال كلها أيها الملك المتسلط المبتلي المغرور

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r4.claim: The Abrahamic maxims counsel guarding one’s time and tongue, speaking little except usefully, and seeking livelihood, provision for the afterlife, and lawful enjoyment.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r4.anchor: وعلى العاقل أن يكون بصيرا بزمانه مقبلا على شأنه حافظا للسانه

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r5.claim: The Prophet calls Moses’s scrolls lessons, challenging the cheerful, laughing, self-assured amid worldly change, strenuous despite destiny, and inactive despite certainty of judgment.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r5.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله: فما كانت صحف موسى قال: كانت عبرا كلها عجبت لمن أيقن بالموت

DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.claim: Asked whether the Prophet received anything from those scrolls, he recited the passage from purification and prayer through the superiority of the afterlife and the scrolls.
DURR-FULL:v8p488/r6.anchor: هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى قال: يا أبا ذر نعم {قد أفلح من تزكى

ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r1.claim: The majority read Ibrāhīm with alif, yāʾ, and kasra on hāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : إبراهيم بألف وبياء والهاء مكسورة

ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r2.speaker: أبو رجاء
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r2.claim: Abū Rajāʾ omits the alif and yāʾ; the source describes the hāʾ vowels as both fatḥa and kasra.
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r2.anchor: وأبو رجاء : بحذفهما والهاء مفتوحة مكسورة معاً

ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r3.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري وابن الزبير
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r3.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī and Ibn al-Zubayr read Abrahām with alif throughout the Qurʾān.
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r3.anchor: وأبو موسى الأشعري وابن الزبير : أبراهام بألف في كل القرآن

ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r4.speaker: مالك بن دينار
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r4.claim: Mālik ibn Dīnār reads Ibrāhīm with alif, fatḥa on hāʾ, and no yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r4.anchor: ومالك بن دينار : إبراهيم بألف وفتح الهاء

ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r5.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakrah reads it with kasra on hāʾ and no yāʾ throughout the Qurʾān.
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r5.anchor: وعبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة : إبراهيم بكسر الهاء

ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r6.speaker: ابن خالويه
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r6.claim: Ibn Khālawayh also records Ibrāhīm with alif and ḍamma on hāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r6.anchor: قال ابن خالويه : وقد جاء إبراهيم ،   يعني بألف وضم الهاء

ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes that the scrolls of Abraham and Moses were discussed earlier in his commentary on Sūrat al-Najm.
ABUHAYYAN:87:19/r7.anchor: وتقدم في والنجم الكلام على صحف إبراهيم وموسى

ALUSI:87:18/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:18/r7.speaker: الأعمش وهرون وعصمة عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI:87:18/r7.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Hārūn, and ʿIṣmah, transmitting from Abū ʿAmr, read al-ṣuḥuf with sukūn on ḥāʾ; this is a Tamīm dialect.
ALUSI:87:18/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وهرون وعصمة كلاهما عن أبي عمرو بسكون الحاء وكذا فيما بعد

ALUSI:87:19/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:19/r1.claim: Abraham and Moses stand in apposition to the earlier scriptures; specifying them after leaving them vague magnifies their importance.
ALUSI:87:19/r1.anchor: وفي إبهامها ووصفها بالقدم ثم بيانها وتفسيرها من تفخيم شأنها

ALUSI:87:19/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:19/r2.claim: Abraham had ten scrolls, and Moses had ten before the Torah; the verse refers to those Mosaic scrolls, not the Torah.
ALUSI:87:19/r2.anchor: وكانت صحف ابراهيم عشرة وكذا صحف موسى عليه السلام والمراد بها ما عدا التوراة

ALUSI:87:19/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:87:19/r3.claim: A report from Abū Dharr to the Prophet says God sent 104 scriptures: 50 to Seth, 30 to Enoch, 10 to Abraham, 10 to Moses before the Torah, besides Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Criterion; al-Ālūsī leaves its authenticity to God.
ALUSI:87:19/r3.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد وابن مردويه وابن عساكر عن أبي ذر قال قلت يا رسول الله كم أنزل الله تعالى من كتاب قال مائة كتابة وأربعة كتب

ALUSI:87:19/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:87:19/r4.claim: The Abrahamic scrolls admonish a ruler not to amass wealth but to answer the oppressed person's plea, even if the oppressed is an unbeliever.
ALUSI:87:19/r4.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله فما كانت صحف ابراهيم قال أمثال كلها أيها الملك المتسلط

ALUSI:87:19/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:87:19/r5.claim: They say a sound-minded person should reserve time for communion with God, self-accounting and reflection, and lawful needs, refreshing the heart for other hours.
ALUSI:87:19/r5.anchor: وعلى العاقل ما لم يكن مغلوباً على عقله أن يكون له ثلاث ساعات ساعة يناجي فيها

ALUSI:87:19/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:87:19/r6.claim: They counsel awareness of one's time, attention to one's affairs, and restraint of the tongue; since speech counts among one's deeds, speak little except about what matters.
ALUSI:87:19/r6.anchor: وعلى العاقل أن يكون بصيراً بزمانه مقبلاً على شأنه حافظاً للسانه فإن من حسب

ALUSI:87:19/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:87:19/r7.claim: They say a wise person should seek livelihood, provision for the afterlife, and permissible enjoyment.
ALUSI:87:19/r7.anchor: وعلى العاقل أن يكون طالباً لثلاث مرمة لمعاش أو تزود لمعاد أو تلذذ

ALUSI:87:19/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:87:19/r8.claim: Moses' scrolls are admonitions: it is astonishing to trust a changing world, rejoice despite certainty of death, laugh despite certainty of Hell, resent destiny despite believing in it, or fail to work despite certainty of reckoning.
ALUSI:87:19/r8.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله فما كانت صحف موسى قال كانت عبرا كلها عجبت لمن أيقن بالموت ثم يفرح

ALUSI:87:19/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:87:19/r9.claim: The Prophet says Qurʾānic teaching given to him from those scrolls includes success for the one who purifies himself, remembers God's name and prays, and that the Hereafter is better than worldly life.
ALUSI:87:19/r9.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى قال يا أبا ذكر نعم

ALUSI:87:19/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r10.speaker: أبو رجاء
ALUSI:87:19/r10.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads Ibrāhīm with alif and yāʾ omitted, and hāʾ reported with either fatḥah or kasrah.
ALUSI:87:19/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء ابرهم بحذف الألف والياء وبالهاء مفتوحة ومكسورة

ALUSI:87:19/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r11.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة
ALUSI:87:19/r11.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakrah reads the name with kasrah on hāʾ only.
ALUSI:87:19/r11.anchor: وعبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة بكسرها لا غير وقرأ أبو موسى الأشعري

ALUSI:87:19/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r12.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري وابن الزبير
ALUSI:87:19/r12.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī and Ibn al-Zubayr read Ibrāhām with an alif in every Qurʾānic occurrence.
ALUSI:87:19/r12.anchor: وقرأ أبو موسى الأشعري وابن الزبير ابراهام بالغين في كل القرآن

ALUSI:87:19/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r13.speaker: مالك بن دينار
ALUSI:87:19/r13.claim: Mālik ibn Dīnār reads Ibrāhim with an alif, fatḥah on hāʾ, and no yāʾ.
ALUSI:87:19/r13.anchor: وقرأ مالك بن دينار ابراهم بألف وفتح الهاء وبغير ياء

ALUSI:87:19/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r14.speaker: ابن خالويه
ALUSI:87:19/r14.claim: Ibn Khālawayh records Ibrahum with ḍamma on hāʾ and neither alif nor yāʾ.
ALUSI:87:19/r14.anchor: وجاء كما قال ابن خالويه ابرهم بضم الهاء بلا ألف ولا ياء

ALUSI:87:19/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:19/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:19/r15.claim: The variants reflect Arab adaptation of foreign names; Abraham is correctly regarded as foreign, though al-Kirmānī offers an Arabic derivation from barhamah, intense looking.
ALUSI:87:19/r15.anchor: وهذا من تصرفات العرب في الأسماء الأعجمية فإن براهيم على الصحيح منها وحكى الكرماني

BAGHAWI:87:19/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:19/r1.speaker: عكرمة والسدي
BAGHAWI:87:19/r1.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Suddi say that this whole sura is found in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.
BAGHAWI:87:19/r1.anchor: قال عكرمة والسدي : هذه السورة في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

BAYDAWI:87:19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:19/r1.claim: “The pages of Abraham and Moses” is an apposition to “the earlier pages.”
BAYDAWI:87:19/r1.anchor: صحف إبراهيم وموسى بدل من الصحف الأولى

BAYDAWI:87:19/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:19/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI:87:19/r2.claim: A closing report promises ten good deeds for each letter God revealed to Abraham, Moses, and Muhammad to whoever recites Sūrat al-Aʿlā.
BAYDAWI:87:19/r2.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من قرأ سورة الأعلى أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد كل حرف أنزله الله

BIQAI:87:19/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:19/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
BIQAI:87:19/r1.claim: Biqāʿī cites a hadith from Abū Dharr to support placing Abraham first because his scriptures are closer to admonition; he gives no grading.
BIQAI:87:19/r1.anchor: قدمه لأن صحفه أقرب إلى الوعظ كما نطق به حديث أبي ذر

BIQAI:87:19/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:19/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:19/r2.claim: Moses is named last because his book is chiefly legal, with fewer admonitions; its forceful warnings include cursing Torah violators and foretelling their violation of its greatest glad tidings about Muhammad.

BIQAI:87:19/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:19/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:19/r3.claim: The order also follows the prophets' chronology and precedence in virtue.
BIQAI:87:19/r3.anchor: مع أن ذكر النبيين عليهما الصلاة والسلام على الأصل في ترتيب الوجود والأفضلية

BIQAI:87:19/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:19/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:19/r4.claim: Tazkiya means cleansing from impurities, attaining transcendence, and acquiring God's qualities to the extent possible.
BIQAI:87:19/r4.anchor: حث آخرها على التزكي وهو التطهر من الأدناس الذي هو معنى التنزه والتخلق بأخلاق الله بحسب الطاقة

BIQAI:87:19/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:19/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:19/r5.claim: Reminding creation of purification shows God did not leave them without guidance or create them aimlessly; purposelessness is a grave imperfection from which He is exalted.
BIQAI:87:19/r5.anchor: إعلام بأن الله تعالى لم يهمل الخلق من البيان بعد أن خلقهم لأنه لم يخلقهم سدى ، لأن ذلك من العبث الذي هو من أكبر النقائص

BIQAI:87:19/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:19/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:19/r6.claim: The sūra's ending returns to its beginning: glorifying God and purifying the soul together form its central purpose.
BIQAI:87:19/r6.anchor: فقد رجع آخرها على أولها ، وكان تنزيه الرب سبحانه وتعالى وتنزيه النفس أيضاً غاية معولها

DURR:87:18/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:18/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that, when these verses were revealed, the Prophet said all of this is contained in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.
DURR:87:18/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : لما نزلت { إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى } قال : رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:87:18/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:18/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says this surah was transcribed from the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; another wording extends the material to al-Najm 53:37 through the end of that surah.
DURR:87:18/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى } قال : نسخت هذه السورة من صحف إبراهيم وموسى

DURR:87:18/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r3.speaker: السدي
DURR:87:18/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says this surah is found in Abraham’s and Moses’ scrolls just as it was revealed to Muhammad.
DURR:87:18/r3.anchor: عن السدي أن هذه السورة في صحف إبراهيم وموسى مثل ما نزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:87:18/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:18/r10.claim: In Abu Dharr’s report, the Prophet’s Abrahamic scroll sayings warn rulers against hoarding, command answering the oppressed even if unbelieving, and commend time for worship, self-examination, lawful needs, careful speech, and lawful provision or enjoyment.
DURR:87:18/r10.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله : فما كانت صحف إبراهيم ؟ قال : أمثال كلها أيها الملك المتسلط المبتلي

DURR:87:18/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:18/r11.claim: The Prophet describes Moses’ scrolls as admonitions against joy despite certainty of death, trust in a changing world, striving despite belief in destiny, and failing to act despite belief in judgment.
DURR:87:18/r11.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله : فما كانت صحف موسى ؟ قال : كانت عبراً كلها عجبت لمن أيقن بالموت

DURR:87:18/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:18/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:87:18/r12.claim: Asked whether any teaching from those scrolls was revealed to him, the Prophet cites the verses from “the one who purifies himself” through this statement about the earlier scrolls.
DURR:87:18/r12.anchor: قلت يا رسول الله : هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ؟ قال : يا أبا ذر نعم

IBNASHUR:87:19/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:19/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:19/r1.claim: “Earlier” means earlier than the Quran, not the first scriptures ever, since some messengers before Abraham reportedly received scrolls.
IBNASHUR:87:19/r1.anchor: والمراد بالأولية في وصف الصحف سبق الزمان بالنسبة إلى القرآن لا التي لم يسبقها غيرها

IBNASHUR:87:19/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:19/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:19/r2.claim: A Bukhārī hadith calls “if you feel no shame, do as you wish” a saying preserved from the earliest prophecy.
IBNASHUR:87:19/r2.anchor: إنَّ مما أدرك الناسُ من كلام النبوءة الأولى

IBNASHUR:87:19/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:19/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNASHUR:87:19/r3.claim: Abū Dharr reports from the Prophet that Abraham’s scrolls numbered ten; Ibn ʿĀshūr names the transmitters but gives no grade.
IBNASHUR:87:19/r3.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن مردويه وابن عساكر وأبو بكر الآجري عن أبي ذر عن رسول الله

IBNATIYYA:87:19/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r1.claim: The majority pronounce the ḥāʾ in al-ṣuḥuf with ḍamma; Hārūn reports Abū ʿAmr with a silent ḥāʾ, also read by al-Aʿmash.
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r1.anchor: روى هارون عن أبي عمرو بسكون الحاء

IBNATIYYA:87:19/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r2.speaker: أبو رجاء
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r2.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads Ibrāhīm without either yāʾ or alif.
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء : { إبراهيم } بغير الياء ولا ألف

IBNATIYYA:87:19/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads the name as Ibrāhām throughout the Qurʾān, as does Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī.
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير «ابراهام » في كل القرآن ، وكذلك أبو موسى الأشعري

IBNATIYYA:87:19/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r4.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakra reads Ibrāhīm with kasra on the hāʾ and without yāʾ throughout the Qurʾān.
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r4.anchor: وقرأ عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة «إبراهِم » بكسر الهاء وبغير ياء في جميع القرآن

IBNATIYYA:87:19/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r5.claim: A report dates Abraham's scriptures to Ramadan's first night, the Torah to its sixth, Psalms to its twelfth, Gospel to its eighteenth, and Qurʾān to its fourteenth.
IBNATIYYA:87:19/r5.anchor: وروي أن { صحف إبراهيم } نزلت في أول ليلة من رمضان ، والتوراة في السادسة من رمضان والزبور في اثني عشرة منه والإنجيل في ثمان عشرة منه والقرآن في أربعة عشرة منه

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet said all this, or this, was in Abraham’s and Moses’ scriptures. Al-Bazzar says he knows no other connected report through trustworthy transmitters on this route except one previously cited.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت : { إِنَّ هَذَا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الأُولَى صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى } قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r2.claim: Al-Nasa’i reports Ibn Abbas saying that all of Surah al-A‘la was in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses; when 53:37 was revealed, he connected Abraham’s fulfillment with the teaching that no bearer bears another’s burden.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت { سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الأَعْلَى } قال : كلها في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ، فلما نزلت : { وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى }

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir takes “this” to refer to the content of 87:14–17: success through purification, remembrance and prayer, the preference for worldly life, and the better, lasting afterlife.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r6.anchor: واختار ابن جرير أن المراد بقوله : { إِنَّ هَذَا } إشارة إلى قوله : { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir calls Ibn Jarir’s reading a good, strong choice.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r7.anchor: وهذا اختيار حسن قوي . وقد روي عن قتادة وابن زيد

IBNKATHIR:87:18/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r8.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r8.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd are also reported to hold the view that “this” refers to the passage about purification, worship, and the preference for the lasting afterlife.
IBNKATHIR:87:18/r8.anchor: وقد روي عن قتادة وابن زيد ، نحوُه . والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet said all this, or this, was in Abraham’s and Moses’ scriptures. Al-Bazzar says he knows no other connected report through trustworthy transmitters on this route except one previously cited.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت : { إِنَّ هَذَا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الأُولَى صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى } قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r2.claim: Al-Nasa’i reports Ibn Abbas saying that all of Surah al-A‘la was in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses; when 53:37 was revealed, he connected Abraham’s fulfillment with the teaching that no bearer bears another’s burden.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت { سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الأَعْلَى } قال : كلها في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ، فلما نزلت : { وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى }

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir links this statement to the scroll teachings in 53:36–42: Abraham’s fulfillment, personal responsibility, human striving and its recompense, and the final return to God.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r3.anchor: يعني أن هذه الآية كقوله في سورة  " النجم "  : { أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَى وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r4.claim: Ikrima identifies “this” as the verses in Surah al-A‘la.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة - في قوله : { إِنَّ هَذَا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الأُولَى صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى } يقول : الآيات التي في سبح اسم ربك الأعلى

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the story of this surah is contained in the earlier scriptures.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r5.anchor: وقال أبو العالية : قصة هذه السورة في الصحف الأولى

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir takes “this” to refer to the content of 87:14–17: success through purification, remembrance and prayer, the preference for worldly life, and the better, lasting afterlife.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r6.anchor: واختار ابن جرير أن المراد بقوله : { إِنَّ هَذَا } إشارة إلى قوله : { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir calls Ibn Jarir’s reading a good, strong choice.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r7.anchor: وهذا اختيار حسن قوي . وقد روي عن قتادة وابن زيد

IBNKATHIR:87:19/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r8.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r8.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd are also reported to hold the view that “this” refers to the passage about purification, worship, and the preference for the lasting afterlife.
IBNKATHIR:87:19/r8.anchor: وقد روي عن قتادة وابن زيد ، نحوُه . والله أعلم

KASHSHAF:87:19/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:19/r1.speaker: أبو ذر
KASHSHAF:87:19/r1.claim: Abū Dharr reports that the Prophet said God sent 104 books: ten scrolls to Adam, fifty to Seth, thirty to Enoch/Idrīs, ten to Abraham, as well as the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Furqān.
KASHSHAF:87:19/r1.anchor: وروي : عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه «أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : كم أنزل الله من كتاب ؟ فقال : مائة وأربعة كتب ،

KASHSHAF:87:19/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:19/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF:87:19/r2.claim: A saying in Abraham’s scrolls advises the wise to guard the tongue, know the age, and attend to one’s own affairs.
KASHSHAF:87:19/r2.anchor: وقيل : إنّ في صحف إبراهيم ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظاً للسانه عارفاً بزمانه

KASHSHAF:87:19/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:19/r3.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF:87:19/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet promises ten good deeds for every letter God sent down to Abraham, Moses, and Muḥammad to whoever recites this sūra.
KASHSHAF:87:19/r3.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " من قرأ سورة الأعلى أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد كل حرف أنزله الله تعالى على إبراهيم وموسى ومحمد "

KASHSHAF:87:19/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:19/r4.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF:87:19/r4.claim: When the Prophet recited the sūra, he would say “Glory to my Lord, the Most High.”
KASHSHAF:87:19/r4.anchor: وكان إذا قرأها قال : سبحان ربي الأعلى وكان علي وابن عباس يقولان ذلك

KASHSHAF:87:19/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:19/r5.speaker: علي وابن عباس
KASHSHAF:87:19/r5.claim: ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās also used to say “Glory to my Lord, the Most High.”
KASHSHAF:87:19/r5.anchor: وكان علي وابن عباس يقولان ذلك

KASHSHAF:87:19/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:19/r6.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF:87:19/r6.claim: The Prophet loved the sūra and said that Michael was the first to say “Glory to my Lord, the Most High.”
KASHSHAF:87:19/r6.anchor: وكان يحبها وقال : أول من قال «سبحان ربي الأعلى » مكيائيل .

NASAFI:87:19/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:19/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:19/r1.claim: “The scrolls of Abraham and Moses” is an apposition to “the earlier scrolls.”
NASAFI:87:19/r1.anchor: { صحف إبراهيم وموسى } بدل من { الصحف الأولى }

NASAFI:87:19/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:19/r2.speaker: الأثر
NASAFI:87:19/r2.claim: A saying transmitted from Abraham's scrolls advises the wise to guard the tongue, know the time, and attend to their affairs.
NASAFI:87:19/r2.anchor: وفي الأثر وفي صحف إبراهيم : ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظاً للسانه عارفاً بزمانه

QURTUBI:87:19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:19/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:19/r1.claim: The scrolls are the books revealed to Abraham and Moses; the exact wording need not occur there, since the same meaning is intended.
QURTUBI:87:19/r1.anchor: يعني الكتب المنزلة عليهما . ولم يرد أن هذه الألفاظ بعينها في تلك الصحف

QURTUBI:87:19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:19/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:19/r2.claim: In al-Ājurrī's report from Abū Dharr, Abraham's scrolls tell a powerful, tested, deluded ruler to defend the oppressed rather than amass wealth; God answers even an unbeliever's plea when oppressed.
QURTUBI:87:19/r2.anchor: فما كانت صحف إبراهيم ؟ قال : كانت أمثالا كلها : أيها الملك المتسلط المبتلى المغرور

QURTUBI:87:19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:19/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:19/r3.claim: The scrolls say a wise person should set aside an hour for communion with God, an hour for self-accounting and reflection on God's favor, and an hour for personal needs such as food and drink.
QURTUBI:87:19/r3.anchor: وعلى العاقل أن يكون له ثلاث

QURTUBI:87:19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:19/r4.claim: They say one should travel only to prepare for the return, maintain one's livelihood, or seek a lawful pleasure, and should understand one's time, attend to one's affairs, and guard one's tongue.
QURTUBI:87:19/r4.anchor: وعلى العاقل ألا يكون ظاعنا إلا في ثلاث : تزود لمعاد ، ومرمة لمعاش

QURTUBI:87:19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:19/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:19/r5.claim: They say that whoever counts speech among deeds speaks little except about what concerns him.
QURTUBI:87:19/r5.anchor: ومن عد كلامه من عمله قل كلامه إلا فيما يعينه

QURTUBI:87:19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:19/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:19/r6.claim: Moses's scrolls wonder that someone certain of death rejoices, someone certain of destiny exhausts himself, or someone who sees the world's reversals feels secure in it.
QURTUBI:87:19/r6.anchor: قال : كانت عبرا كلها : عجبت لمن أيقن بالموت كيف يفرح ! وعجبت لمن أيقن بالقدر

QURTUBI:87:19/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:19/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:19/r7.claim: They also wonder that someone certain of tomorrow's reckoning fails to act.
QURTUBI:87:19/r7.anchor: وعجبت لمن أيقن بالحساب غدا ثم هو لا يعمل !

QURTUBI:87:19/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:19/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:19/r8.claim: Asked whether anything from those scrolls remains in what God revealed to the Prophet, he answers yes and recites this sūra's verses on purification, prayer, preferring this world, and the enduring afterlife.
QURTUBI:87:19/r8.anchor: فهل في أيدينا شيء مما كان في يديه إبراهيم وموسى ، مما أنزل الله عليك ؟ قال : نعم اقرأ يا أبا ذر

RAZI:87:19/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:19/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:19/r1.claim: One grammatical view makes “the scriptures of Abraham and Moses” an apposition explaining “the earlier scriptures.”
RAZI:87:19/r1.anchor: أنه بيان لقوله : { في الصحف الأولى }

RAZI:87:19/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:19/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:19/r2.claim: Another view says the teaching is mentioned in the scriptures of all prophets, including those of Abraham and Moses.
RAZI:87:19/r2.anchor: أن المراد أنه مذكور في صحف جميع الأنبياء التي منها صحف إبراهيم وموسى

RAZI:87:19/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:19/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
RAZI:87:19/r3.claim: Abū Dharr reports that the Prophet counted 104 revealed books: ten to Adam, fifty to Seth, thirty to Idrīs, ten to Abraham, then the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Furqān.
RAZI:87:19/r3.anchor: روي عن أبي ذر أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كم أنزل الله من كتاب ؟

RAZI:87:19/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:19/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI:87:19/r4.claim: A report says Abraham’s scriptures taught that a wise person should guard his tongue, know his time, and attend to his own affairs.
RAZI:87:19/r4.anchor: وقيل : إن في صحف إبراهيم : ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه

BURHAN:v2p38/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p38/r13.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
BURHAN:v2p38/r13.claim: Al-Rāzī says erased recitation and script result when God causes people to forget it and orders them to stop reciting and writing it, as with earlier scriptures; no Qur'anic passage can be abrogated after the Prophet's death.
BURHAN:v2p38/r13.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الرازي نسخ الرسم والتلاوة إنما يكون بأن ينسيهم الله إياه ويرفعه من أوهامهم ويأمرهم بالإعراض عن تلاوته وكتبه في المصحف

ITQAN:v3p69/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p69/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
ITQAN:v3p69/r2.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi says abrogation of written text and recitation occurs through divinely induced forgetting, so the wording fades like earlier scriptures; any such abrogation must occur by the Prophet's death, since Qur'an cannot be abrogated afterward.
ITQAN:v3p69/r2.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الرازي نسخ الرسم والتلاوة إنما يكون بأن ينسيهم الله إياه ويرفعه من أوهامهم ويأمرهم بالإعراض عن تلاوته وكتبه في المصحف فيندرس

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r3.speaker: واثلة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r3.claim: Wathila reports the Prophet's chronology of scripture revelation: the Suhuf of Abraham on Ramadan's first night, the Torah on day six, the Gospel on day thirteen, the Psalms on day eighteen, and the Quran on day twenty-four.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p15/r3.anchor: عن واثلة أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: "نزلت صحف إبراهيم أول ليلة من رمضان، وأنزلت التوراة

BURHAN:v3p239#4/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r5.claim: Precedence by time can combine with honor, as in these ordered lists of chosen figures and scriptures.
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r5.anchor: واعلم أنه ينضم إليه مع ذلك التشريف كقوله ﴿ إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران ﴾

ITQAN:v3p38/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p38/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p38/r1.claim: Order can follow revelation chronology, as in naming the scriptures of Abraham and Moses or placing Torah and Gospel before the Criterion.
ITQAN:v3p38/r1.anchor: أو باعتبار الإنزال كقوله ﴿ صحف إبراهيم وموسى ﴾

ITQAN:v4p535#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the verse about this teaching being in the earlier scriptures was revealed, the Prophet said that this, or all of it, was in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
ITQAN:v4p535#3/r2.anchor: وأخرج البزار عن ابن عباس قال لما نزلت ﴿ إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى ﴾ قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASHR:v2p399#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p399#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p399#2/r1.claim: Imāla of the rhyme endings from al-Aʿlā through Mūsā was covered earlier in the chapter on imāla.
NASHR:v2p399#2/r1.anchor: تقدم إمالة رءوس آيها من لدن الأعلى إلى وموسى في باب الإمالة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.claim: Disbelievers prefer transient life to the better, eternal afterlife, so the Prophet's message finds no root in their hearts despite its continuity with earlier prophetic teaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p271/r3.anchor: giving preference to this world over the next

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r3.claim: The Prophet's teaching is not new: earlier revelation taught that the Hereafter is real life and each soul bears its own deeds and burden.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p280/r3.anchor: whatever the Prophet (sws) is telling his addressees is not something new or unique

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r1.claim: Moses' and Israelite prophets' scriptures survive in the Bible despite substantial alteration; they still clearly teach monotheism and the Hereafter and can revive faith.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r1.anchor: all of these very clearly and very effectively depict the teachings of monotheism and life in the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r2.claim: Abraham left oral exhortations rather than a scripture; his Israelite descendants preserved the teachings in writing, and their prophets renewed them, with evidence still present in scripture and the Qur'an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r2.anchor: did not leave a scripture for the guidance of his people

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r3.claim: The unlettered Ishmaelites preserved Abraham's teaching orally for a time, then lost it to neglect and innovations; Muhammad revived and completed it as God's enduring perfect religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p281/r3.anchor: these teachings were not only revived, they were also completed

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r1.speaker: majority
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r1.claim: Most commentators date al-Aʿlā early Makkan; it is often placed eighth chronologically, after al-Takwīr.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r1.anchor: the majority maintain that it is early Makkan

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r3.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r3.claim: Another view holds the whole surah Makkan, since it may refer to the rituals before they were formally instituted.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r3.anchor: Others say that it can still refer to these ritual practices

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r4.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r4.claim: The Prophet is said to recommend surahs 87 and 88 for the evening prayer and often recited them at both Eids and Friday prayer.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r4.anchor: The Prophet is said to have recommended reciting Sūrahs 87 and 88 for the evening prayer

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r5.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r5.claim: The Prophet is also said to advise reciting the surah while prostrating.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r5.anchor: advised his followers to recite it while in prostration

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r6.speaker: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r6.claim: In Shiite tradition, ʿAlī says one who recites it has in effect recited the Quran and scriptures of Moses and Abraham; its blessing merits daily recitation.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r6.anchor: according to Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, if people knew what a blessing al-Aʿlā has

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r7.claim: The surah moves from glorification and encouragement to contrasting hearers, rebuking worldly preference, and affirming continuity with earlier revelation.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r7.anchor: It concludes with a sharp rebuke of those who prefer this world (vv. 16–17)
